title: Model sourcing cost-velocity matrix and contractual risk stressor test
creator: Priya Nair
description: Objective: Build a decision surface (matrix + playbook) that maps regional model supply velocity and pricing shocks to recommended contractual and runtime responses. Scope includes: data collection (availability, measured latency, per-token cost across regions/providers), stressor scenario definitions (short-term outage, price spike, forced deprecation of a model family), quantitative decision thresholds, and a runnable playbook for PMs and SREs to trigger procurement, rollout, and fallback actions. Deliverables: 1) a CSV matrix (region x model variant x stressor) with recommended action and estimated delta cost; 2) a step-by-step playbook for procurement & ops; 3) Console rules to surface alerts and automated partial-failover policies; 4) a short field-probe plan to validate matrix assumptions with 3 pilot customers.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix populated with historical and synthetic stressor data for top 8 regions and 12 model variants
Decision thresholds documented and testable in staging (simulated outage + price spike)
Playbook includes contractual trigger language and a runbook for on-call ops (SLO impact, rollback criteria)
Console alerting rule and one automated fallback policy implemented in staging and demoable
At least one pilot customer field-probe scheduled and kickoff notes recorded
risks_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs: aggressive fallback to smaller quantized variants reduces cost but can increase hallucination risk for retrieval-augmented workflows. Locking procurement commitments reduces price volatility but increases overprovision cost if supply stabilizes. We must balance enterprise SLA expectations vs PLG cost sensitivity. Risk: inaccurate supply signals could trigger unnecessary contract upgrades; mitigation is 'double-confirm' step in playbook and short-term probes before long-term committed purchases.
